A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BridgePolicy and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Matching content across relocation and renumbering supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations on 52 simulation tasks and five real-world robot tasks, together with ablations and empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds an evaluation of L1 versus L2 reconstruction objectives in Appendix F.4.

M1.justification: The bridge SDE, cross-attention fusion, contrastive alignment, default L1 reconstruction objective, and sampling procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. The added L2 experiment is an ablation, not a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Adroit, DexArt, and MetaWorld tasks and five real-world tasks. Table 1's caption changes from 50 to 52 tasks, correcting its agreement with the existing task coverage rather than adding tasks.

E2.justification: The simulation baseline suite remains DP, DP3, Simple DP3, FlowPolicy, and VITA; the real-world suite also remains unchanged. New Table 12 adds an L2/MSE-trained BridgePolicy variant as an internal comparator to the default L1/MAE formulation.

E3.justification: Appendix F.4 introduces a controlled comparison varying the reconstruction objective on three Adroit tasks. Existing training budgets, checkpoint selection, evaluation episodes, and sampling-step settings remain unchanged. New simulation hyperparameters in Table 8 document existing settings rather than establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: V3 adds the L1-versus-L2 loss ablation in Appendix F.4 and Table 12, which v2 mentioned but did not actually report. Existing sample-efficiency, fusion, policy-head, hyperparameter, perturbation, and real-world case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix F.5 explicitly identifies the reported statistics as mean and standard deviation over three random seeds; v2 F.4 stated only that results were averaged over three seeds. Both already reported three seeds and uncertainty values, so no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Reported uncertainty changes substantially across the simulation results. In Table 1, BridgePolicy's MetaWorld Easy result changes from 0.91±0.24 to 0.91±0.03 and Very Hard from 0.79±0.32 to 0.79±0.02, materially changing the portrayed precision. Numerous per-task uncertainties also change, while all matched simulation means and real-world scores remain unchanged. New Table 12 reports L1/L2 averages of 0.81/0.80; these are added ablation results, not improved benchmark performance.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 in Section 3.2 and Appendix B now explicitly requires identical sampling noise for the original and perturbed trajectories. This clarifies the condition already used to cancel noise in the proof; the bound and remaining derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain observation-informed bridge sampling, alignment of heterogeneous observations with actions, and superior performance over the same task coverage. Emphasizing the semantic aligner consolidates the previous fusion/alignment description without changing these claims' functional scope.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 newly states that BRIDGER's performance depends heavily on its coarse policy's quality. Interpretations of BridgePolicy's experimental findings and the stated limitation concerning SDE sampling and one-step distillation otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project/code-access link in the abstract and a simulation hyperparameter table specifying settings such as batch size 256, horizon 8, 100 training timesteps, and learning rate 1e-4. These expand documentation; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 now explicitly describes BRIDGER's refinement as a diffusion bridge and emphasizes coarse-policy dependence, while sharpening the contrast with VITA's latent-space decoder. The cited-work set is unchanged; the UniDB++ reference receives only a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized introduction and related-work rewrites, replaces several uses of multi-modal with heterogeneous, and adds the loss-ablation subsection. Affiliations, publication text, running headers, and acknowledgment/impact-statement ordering change, while the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds two tables, reformats visual panels, and redisplays existing appendix task examples as main-text Figures 5–6. V2 Figure 12 moves to main-text Figure 7, and other displays shift accordingly. These are limited presentation changes rather than new task or case-study evidence.

improvement.justification: V3 supplies the loss ablation promised but absent in v2, states the stability theorem's shared-noise premise, and adds simulation settings and code-access information. These modestly improve completeness and reproducibility. The unexplained uncertainty revisions cannot be credited as stronger empirical evidence; the main mean results and claims remain unchanged.
